errors.text_span: The slices are labeled “3.3%,” “10.1%,” “45.9%,” and “40.6%," displayed in colors green, pink, yellow, and light blue, respectively.
errors.evidence: This description incorrectly uses the percentage values as labels for the slices. Furthermore, the mapping of colors to these percentages is incorrect. For example, the 3.3% slice (label N+K-) is reddish-orange, not green. The 40.6% slice (label N+K+) is teal/green, not light blue.
The description for the 'easy' and 'medium' charts completely omits any mention of the legend or the actual categorical labels for the slices (N+K+, N-K+, N-K-, N+K-).
The descriptions for all three charts fail to mention their individual titles: "easy", "medium", and "hard".

errors.text_span: colored pink, light blue, yellow, and orange, representing “44.3%,” “7.2%,” “3.9%,” and “44.6%," respectively.
errors.evidence: The mapping of colors and percentages for the middle chart is completely incorrect. For example, it assigns 'pink' to 44.3%, which is actually the yellow slice (N-K+). It assigns 'orange' to 44.6%, which is the teal slice (N+K+).

errors.text_span: The categories are visually arranged from the largest to smallest slice.
errors.evidence: This is incorrect. The slices in the middle chart are ordered (clockwise from top) as 44.6%, 44.3%, 7.2%, 3.9%. This is not a simple largest-to-smallest arrangement.
The 'hard' pie chart clearly shows four slices, not five.
The description hallucinates 'CoT' as a fifth slice in the 'hard' chart. 'CoT' is a text label located underneath the middle chart, not a category within any of the pie charts.

The list of proportions is incorrectly mapped to the labels mentioned previously in the sentence. For example, the first label mentioned is 'N+K+', but the first proportion listed is 36.2%, whereas the chart shows N+K+ is 20.1%. Additionally, it includes 3.9%, which is a value from the middle chart, not the 'hard' chart.
